title: Midroll VAST 4.1 audio with Pricing, bitrate ladder and VideoClicks, adapted from IAB's own sample

source.name: IAB Audio_DAAST_Sample: VAST 4.1 adType=audio, not DAAST XML
source.license: Repository LICENSE contains a disclaimer only; adapted structurally, all identifiers/text rewritten
source.notes: All source records are retained in assets/sources.json by reference.sourceIds (video-audio:va-audio-sample-caution, video-audio:va-sample-license).

modifications: The upstream sample's root element is <VAST>, not <DAAST>, despite its filename — verified by reading the raw XML: root tag, adType="audio" attribute and Pricing/AdServingId/AdTitle/Creatives structure all match VAST 4.1, none match a DAAST 1.0 root. This fixture keeps that same VAST 4.1 shape.

Corrected: the upstream sample types all three of its bitrate-ladder MediaFile entries video/mp4 with width/height/codec=FLAC on an audio-typed Ad — an internal inconsistency in the public sample. This fixture retypes all three MediaFile entries audio/mpeg, codec MP3, width=0 height=0, to make the creative internally consistent with adType="audio".
One upstream Tracking URL used http://; every tracking/click/media URL here is https:// on a .test host.
All IDs, domains, titles and tracking/media hosts are original synthetic test data; the upstream Extensions/iab-Count block was dropped as immaterial to audio validation.
Request/response IDs and impid are intentionally paired; no real person, cookie, advertising ID, IP address or live tracking endpoint is retained.
provenance.sanitized: No production payload or PII used. All resource and tracking hosts end in .test; external network must remain blocked.

pairApplicability.note: Use x-openrtb-version: 2.6 when replaying HTTP; envelope itself has no version field.

specNotes: IAB's own VAST_Samples repository names this fixture Audio_DAAST_Sample.xml, but its root element is <VAST version="4.1">, not <DAAST> — the filename is misleading, already noted in audio-inapp-26-podcast-companion. adType="audio" is VAST's own way of marking an audio-typed Ad.
VAST allows a bitrate ladder (multiple MediaFile entries at different bitrates for the same creative) exactly as shown here; nothing in VAST 4.1 requires a single MediaFile.

VALID_MF_TYPES in rules-vast.js only lists video container MIME types; audio/mpeg is not on that allow-list, so every audio MediaFile triggers vast.mediafile_type_invalid regardless of otherwise-valid VAST structure (same root cause as DEF-101 on the simpler single-MediaFile audio fixtures).

Any VAST-shaped adm on an audio bid is still tagged FORMATS.VIDEO by format-detect.js's unconditional isVastShape sniff, producing format.formats=[audio,video] instead of [audio] — same DEF-101 cause.
Validity describes protocol structure and declared constraints; generated media bytes must be checked against declared MIME/duration before playback tests.
Current Inspector contract displays VAST as inert XML; text visibility must not be counted as creative rendering or media playback.
notes: Core observations in the source archive were deliberately excluded from expectations. Protocol metadata may describe a vendor-specific 2.x carrier; it does not claim a normative minor-version inference.

preview.capabilityGap: The current VAST preview is inert XML; audio playback and bitrate-ladder MediaFile selection are not implemented.

knownGap.note: Audio VAST and audio MediaFiles must remain valid and be identified as audio; optional request Device attributes do not invalidate the pair.
